transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I can’t stop thinking about how bad I look, especially my face and stomach, and it’s gotten to where I don’t want people to see me anymore. It's just really embarrassing to even be out of the house.
When you avoid going out, is it mainly because you feel ashamed of specific flaws in your appearance, or because you fear people will judge or embarrass you in social situations more generally?

It’s definitely because of how I look, specifically my face and my stomach. I’m just so ashamed of those areas, and I'm convinced that if I go to church or farm meetings, people will just stare and judge those exact flaws. It’s not a general fear of being around people, I just can’t stand the thought of them seeing how bad I look now.
Do you ever think your face or stomach only seem flawed to you and might not look that way to other people, or are you completely certain they are truly deformed? How convinced are you of that?

My wife and pastor swear they can't see what I'm talking about, but it's impossible to believe them when I look in the mirror. The sagginess, blotchiness, and my stomach look so obviously bad to me that I'm completely convinced these flaws are real and highly noticeable. I just know deep down that anyone who looks at me is going to stare and judge how awful I look.
Do you spend a lot of time checking these areas in mirrors, grooming, comparing yourself to others, or trying to hide them? About how many hours a day do these thoughts and behaviors take up?

Yes, my mind circles back to these thoughts all day long, and I easily spend hours on these habits. I catch myself going to the bathroom mirror every half hour to pull at the skin on my cheeks and poke at my stomach, often changing shirts multiple times while constantly asking my wife or daughter for reassurance.

Has there ever been a time when you thought these appearance concerns might be exaggerated or not as noticeable to others, or are you always completely certain they are real? Even briefly, do you ever doubt your belief about how you look?

No, I don't really have any doubt about it. Even though my wife, daughter, and pastor constantly reassure me and say they don't see what I'm talking about, looking in the mirror is an undeniable reality for me. I remain completely convinced these flaws are real and that others will notice and judge them, despite what my family says.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (face and stomach) that others do not see, accompanied by repetitive appearance-related behaviors (frequent mirror checking, skin pulling/poking, changing shirts, reassurance seeking), marked shame and avoidance of leaving home, and poor/absent insight with delusional-level conviction that the defects are real. The concern is specifically appearance-based rather than a generalized social fear, supporting body dysmorphic disorder within ICD-10 hypochondriacal disorder/somatiform framework.
